stream: D (construct relevance and flag stability), revision round 1, post-review exploratory

definitions.pool: Design A pool: students with >= 200 confidence-tagged responses (S1 n = 1,389; S2 n = 554). Same students at every N.
definitions.N: Number of confidence-tagged responses in ONE score. Split-half values: score on N responses, estimated from two N/2 halves with Spearman-Brown. Disjoint-set values: each of the two sets has N responses, no step-up.
definitions.bias: mean(c) - mean(x), c = Confidence/100 in {0, .25, .5, .75, 1}, x = correctness. Positive = overconfident.
definitions.conf: mean confidence of the N responses (0-1 scale).
definitions.acc: proportion correct of the N responses.
definitions.splithalf_SB: Paper machinery (reliability.subsample_matrix + half_indices + sb_mean): one N-subsample per student (seed [42, 5, N, sid]), 50 random splits (random) or first vs second half by date (temporal), Pearson r across students, Spearman-Brown 2r/(1+r), mean over splits. Values at N in the original grid equal the baseline curves (regression gate).
definitions.disjoint_sets: rev_round2 design: per repeat, 2N responses drawn without replacement per student (seed [42, 92, N, sid]); set A = first N, set B = last N. 50 repeats. Flags and the decomposition use these N-response scores.
definitions.r_parallel_*: Pearson r between set A and set B scores, mean over repeats: a direct parallel-forms reliability at N (no Spearman-Brown). Cross-check of splithalf_SB.
definitions.var_true_*, cov_true_conf_acc: Cross-set covariances (set A with set B), averaged over repeats. Because the sets share no response, these estimate between-student true-score (co)variances at volume N. Identity: var_true_bias = var_true_conf + var_true_acc - 2 cov_true_conf_acc (residual stored).
definitions.true_share_conf / true_share_acc / true_: var_true_conf / var_true_bias, var_true_acc / var_true_bias, -2 cov_true_conf_acc / var_true_bias. Sum to 1. Shares above 1 mean the component's stable variance exceeds that of bias and is cancelled by the positive conf-acc covariance.
definitions.true_attrib_conf / true_attrib_acc: Covariance attribution of the stable bias variance: cov_true(bias, conf) / var_true_bias = (var_true_conf - cov_true_conf_acc) / var_true_bias and cov_true(bias, -acc) / var_true_bias = (var_true_acc - cov_true_conf_acc) / var_true_bias. Sum to 1; each is the part of the stable between-student bias variance carried by that component.
definitions.obs_*: Same decompositions on observed (same-set) variances; include measurement error.
definitions.rho_true_bias_conf, rho_true_bias_acc, r: Disattenuated (true-score) correlations from the cross-set covariances. rho_true_bias_conf^2 = share of stable bias variance linearly accounted for by stable confidence alone.
definitions.r_obs_*_sameset: Correlations within one set (part-whole: bias contains conf and acc, so these are not independent evidence).
definitions.r_cross_bias_conf / r_cross_bias_acc: Raw correlation of bias in one N-set with conf (acc) in the other N-set, symmetrized. Not the same quantity as the submitted .351 / -.279, which are 10-response half scores (rev_extras, N = 20 split).

flag rules.decile: top 10% of bias in the set (k = round(.10 n)), argsort order for ties; identical to rev_round2.
flag rules.thr15: bias > +.15 (strict), computed on integers: 25 sum(code) - 100 sum(x) > 15 N.
flag rules.thr20: bias > +.20 (strict), same integer rule with 20 N.
flag rules.lcb_z: lower bound of the two-sided 95% CI of the student's bias above 0: mean(d) - 1.96 sd(d) / sqrt(N) > 0, d = c - x, sd with ddof 1. sd = 0 sets: bound = mean, flagged iff mean > 0 (counts in set_properties).
flag rules.lcb_t: same with the t quantile, df = N - 1 (sensitivity).
flag rules.ci_three_way_z: over = lcb_z > 0, under = upper bound < 0, else unclassified; agreement and Cohen's kappa across sets.

flag metrics.share_flagged: share of students flagged in a set (mean of the two sets, mean over repeats).
flag metrics.retention: 2 |A and B| / (|A| + |B|) (Dice), mean over repeats. Equals the submitted top-decile retention |A and B| / k when both sets have k flags.
flag metrics.retention_directional: P(flag in other set | flag in this set), both directions pooled.
flag metrics.chance_retention: expected retention if the two sets' flags were independent: 2 |A| |B| / (n (|A| + |B|)); about equal to share_flagged.
flag metrics.kappa: Cohen's kappa of the binary flag across the two sets (agreement beyond chance, both flagged and not flagged).
flag metrics.share_flagged_with_other_set_bias_le_0: among flags, share whose bias in the other set is <= 0 (not overconfident at all on fresh data).

definitions.bootstrap: Percentile 95% CI, B = 1000 student resamples, the joint draws of reliability.py (seed [42, 77, sid]); the same resample is applied to every statistic and every N, with subsamples, splits and disjoint sets held fixed. Bias split-half CIs at original grid N equal the baseline curve CIs (regression gate).
definitions.rho2_true_bias_conf / rho2_true_bias_acc: Squares of rho_true_bias_conf / rho_true_bias_acc: share of stable bias variance linearly accounted for by stable confidence (accuracy) alone. Computed in r1_D_report.py from the stored point values (no CI).

decision_rule.basis: Reliability anchors already used in the submitted manuscript: .70 minimally acceptable for research use, .80 lower-stakes applied interpretation (Nunnally, 1978), about .90 for decisions with individual consequences (AERA et al., 2014). Applied to the Design A random-split bias reliability at N (point estimate); the labeling rule uses the temporal split because a label assumes stability over time.

tiers.guidance: Individual scores not interpretable; only aggregate (class or cohort) use remains, and the reliability of aggregates was not estimated here. Do not report individual scores.
Research use of individual scores in correlational or group-comparison analyses; do not show individual scores or labels to students or teachers.
Low-stakes individual feedback: show the score with its uncertainty band as a provisional description; no 'overconfident' label.

decision_rule.labeling: An individual 'overconfident' or 'underconfident' label is treated as a classification with individual consequences and requires temporal-split bias reliability >= .90. The maximum temporal-split bias reliability over the whole Design A grid (N <= 200) is stored per sample; if it is below .90, no N in these data supports individual labeling.
decision_rule.caveat: Group-level reliability (of class or cohort means) was NOT computed in this stream; the 'group' tier rests on averaging over students, not on a computed coefficient.
decision_rule.known_asymmetries: Tiers use the random-split point estimate. Temporal-split bias r at N = 30 is .750 (S1) and .747 (S2), below the .80 feedback cut. Bootstrap intervals straddle a cut at S1 N = 15 (.70), S2 N = 15 (.70) and S2 N = 30 (.80). The choice of split and of point vs interval is left to the writer.
